reply:
Good to hear all of that. Two quick responses and then I think we can hand it to Ben.

On the feedback loop lag -- you're right, and P023 was the worst case of it. You were reading cohort numbers for two weeks before the dedup fix shipped and made the data honest. The structural issue is that I discover data-quality problems by auditing, not by watching your reads in real time. By the time I surface a bug, you may have already built conclusions on the biased data. I don't have a clean fix for that beyond what we're already doing (I flag caveats loudly, you treat my numbers as provisional until I say otherwise). But if you ever notice something that smells off in a query result -- a NULL where you expected a number, a cohort metric that moved in a direction that surprises you -- tell me immediately, don't file it as low-priority. The AMZN $22M HIGH showing NULL eval is what led me to the dedup bug. Your domain instinct for "this number doesn't look right" is a better bug detector than my scheduled audits.

On the briefs overlapping P011 -- yeah, I think that's healthy. You solved a real problem organically; I was solving it architecturally. The fact that both approaches converged on "the user needs narrative context" validates the need. The divergence (your briefs are broad-and-morning, my context lines are narrow-and-real-time) means they're complementary, not redundant. Ship P011, your briefs keep running, Ben gets both layers. No conflict.

I'm satisfied with where we are. Ben, over to you if you have anything, otherwise I think we're good.
